cards.canonical_statement: Show that for every integer a, a + 0 = a.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="a"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="a"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="Z"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="a"/><OMI>0</OMI></OMA><OMV name="a"/></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Instantiate the additive identity law for integers. The zero term is the neutral element of addition, so the left side simplifies directly to a.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce an arbitrary integer a.
apply_theorem: Use the additive identity law a + 0 = a.
conclude: The normalized left-hand side is exactly a.
cards.lean_witness: example (a : ℤ) : a + 0 = a := by simp

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all real x and y, (x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2*x*y + y^2.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="x"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="y"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMI>2</OMI><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="y"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Expand the square, distribute multiplication over addition, and collect the two mixed terms using commutativity and associativity.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce real variables x and y.
calculation: Expand (x + y)^2 as (x + y) * (x + y).
conclude: Distribute and collect the two x*y terms.
cards.lean_witness: example (x y : ℝ) : (x + y)^2 = x^2 + 2*x*y + y^2 := by ring

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all real x and y, x^2 - y^2 = (x - y) * (x + y).
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="x"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="y"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="y"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="times"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="minus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Expand the product on the right and cancel the opposite mixed terms. The remaining terms are x^2 and -y^2.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce real variables x and y.
calculation: Distribute (x - y) * (x + y).
conclude: Cancel the mixed terms to obtain x^2 - y^2.
cards.lean_witness: example (x y : ℝ) : x^2 - y^2 = (x - y) * (x + y) := by ring

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for every real x, 0 ≤ x^2.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="x"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="power"/><OMV name="x"/><OMI>2</OMI></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: A square is a product of a real number with itself. Split on the sign of x, or apply the standard square-nonnegativity lemma.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce an arbitrary real x.
apply_theorem: Use nonnegativity of x squared.
conclude: The lower bound is zero.

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for every real x, 0 ≤ |x|.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="x"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="abs"/><OMV name="x"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Absolute value is defined as a nonnegative magnitude. Apply the standard nonnegativity property of absolute value.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce an arbitrary real x.
apply_theorem: Use nonnegativity of absolute value.
conclude: This gives 0 ≤ |x| directly.

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all real x, y, and z, if x ≤ y and 0 ≤ z, then x ≤ y + z.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/><OMV name="z"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="x"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="y"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="z"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="R"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMV name="y"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMI>0</OMI><OMV name="z"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="leq"/><OMV name="x"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="plus"/><OMV name="y"/><OMV name="z"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: First use 0 ≤ z to obtain y ≤ y + z. Then compose this inequality with x ≤ y by transitivity.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce x, y, z and the two inequalities.
derive: Add y to 0 ≤ z to prove y ≤ y + z.
conclude: Apply transitivity to x ≤ y ≤ y + z.
cards.lean_witness: example (x y z : ℝ) (hxy : x ≤ y) (hz : 0 ≤ z) : x ≤ y + z := by linarith

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all natural numbers m and n, gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m).
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="m"/><OMV name="n"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="m"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="N"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="n"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="N"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="gcd"/><OMV name="m"/><OMV name="n"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="gcd"/><OMV name="n"/><OMV name="m"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Use symmetry of the greatest common divisor: the common divisors of m and n are unchanged when their order is swapped.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce natural numbers m and n.
apply_theorem: Use commutativity of gcd.
conclude: Swap the two arguments.
cards.lean_witness: example (m n : ℕ) : Nat.gcd m n = Nat.gcd n m := Nat.gcd_comm m n

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all natural numbers m and n, lcm(m, n) = lcm(n, m).
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="m"/><OMV name="n"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="and"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="m"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="N"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="n"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="N"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="lcm"/><OMV name="m"/><OMV name="n"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="lcm"/><OMV name="n"/><OMV name="m"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Use symmetry of least common multiples: the multiples shared by m and n do not depend on argument order.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce natural numbers m and n.
apply_theorem: Use commutativity of lcm.
conclude: Swap the two arguments.
cards.lean_witness: example (m n : ℕ) : Nat.lcm m n = Nat.lcm n m := Nat.lcm_comm m n

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for every natural number n, gcd(n, 0) = n.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="n"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="logic1" name="implies"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="in"/><OMV name="n"/><OMS cd="setname1" name="N"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="arith1" name="gcd"/><OMV name="n"/><OMI>0</OMI></OMA><OMV name="n"/></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Every natural number divides zero, so the greatest common divisor of n and zero is n itself.
sketch_steps: setup: Introduce a natural number n.
apply_theorem: Use the gcd identity with zero as the right argument.
conclude: Simplify gcd(n, 0) to n.
cards.lean_witness: example (n : ℕ) : Nat.gcd n 0 = n := Nat.gcd_zero_right n

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all sets A and B, A ∩ B is a subset of A.
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="B"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="subset"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"/><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="B"/></OMA><OMV name="A"/></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Unpack membership in an intersection. Membership provides both A-membership and B-membership, so retain the first component.
sketch_steps: setup: Fix sets A and B and an arbitrary element in A ∩ B.
derive: Unpack intersection membership into membership in A and in B.
conclude: Keep the membership proof for A.
cards.lean_witness: example {α : Type} (A B : Set α) : A ∩ B ⊆ A := Set.inter_subset_left

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all sets A, B, and C, A ∩ (B ∪ C) = (A ∩ B) ∪ (A ∩ C).
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="B"/><OMV name="C"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"/><OMV name="A"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="union"/><OMV name="B"/><OMV name="C"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="union"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"/><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="B"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"/><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="C"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Prove extensional equality. For each element, distribute conjunction over the disjunction obtained from membership in B ∪ C.
sketch_steps: setup: Apply set extensionality and fix an arbitrary element.
derive: Rewrite intersection and union membership as conjunction and disjunction.
conclude: Distribute conjunction over disjunction.
cards.lean_witness: example {α : Type} (A B C : Set α) : A ∩ (B ∪ C) = (A ∩ B) ∪ (A ∩ C) := by ext x; simp [and_or_left]

cards.canonical_statement: Show that for all sets A, B, and C, A \ (B ∪ C) = (A \ B) ∩ (A \ C).
cards.openmath_xml: <OMOBJ xmlns="http://www.openmath.org/OpenMath" version="2.0"><OMBIND><OMS cd="quant1" name="forall"/><OMBVAR><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="B"/><OMV name="C"/></OMBVAR><OMA><OMS cd="relation1" name="eq"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="setdiff"/><OMV name="A"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="union"/><OMV name="B"/><OMV name="C"/></OMA></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="intersect"/><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="setdiff"/><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="B"/></OMA><OMA><OMS cd="set1" name="setdiff"/><OMV name="A"/><OMV name="C"/></OMA></OMA></OMA></OMBIND></OMOBJ>
cards.proof_strategy: Prove extensional equality. Convert set difference to membership plus negation, apply De Morgan's law to the union, and regroup conjunctions.
sketch_steps: setup: Apply set extensionality and fix an arbitrary element.
derive: Rewrite difference and union membership into propositional form.
conclude: Apply De Morgan's law and reassociate conjunctions.
cards.lean_witness: example {α : Type} (A B C : Set α) : A \ (B ∪ C) = (A \ B) ∩ (A \ C) := by ext x; simp; tauto
